'''Cacaopera''' is an extinct [[Misumalpan languages|Misumalpan]] language formerly spoken in the department of Morazán in [[El Salvador]] by the [[Cacaopera people]]. It was closely related to [[Matagalpa language|Matagalpa]], and slightly more distantly to [[Sumo languages|Sumo]], but was geographically separated from other Misumalpan languages.

The last [[semi-speaker]]s of Cacaopera lived in the 1970s; none of them native speakers,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ailla.utexas.org/search/resource.html?r_id=2551|title=MesoAmerican Languages Collection of Lyle Campbell|last=Campbell|first=Lyle|date=1973|website=Archive of the Indigenous Language of Latin America|publisher=University of Texas at Austin|access-date=May 2, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160701174202/http://www.ailla.utexas.org/search/resource.html?r_id=2551|archive-date=July 1, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Campbell |first=Lyle |date=1975 |title=Cacaopera |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/30027563 |journal=Anthropological Linguistics |volume=17 |issue=4 |pages=146–153 |issn=0003-5483}}</ref> the last of them died in 1974.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Cacaoperas o kakawiras – Ruta de Paz |url=https://rutadepaz.com/cacaoperas-o-kakawiras/ |access-date=2026-05-07 |language=es}}</ref>
